_about: Every behaviour the fake Spotify models, labelled by how it is known. docs-only: from Spotify's documentation (references, changelogs, announcements) alone. checked-live: confirmed against real Spotify too; 'checked' says how. Each names the scenario (harness/scenarios/) a live replay checks it with, or says why none can. tests/test_scenarios.py keeps this file and the scenarios in step. A passing live replay makes a scenario's behaviours checked-live.

behaviours.summary: A playlist's items come 20 to a page by default, at most 50.
behaviours.label: docs-only

behaviours.summary: A limit of 0 is refused, though the schema allows it.
behaviours.label: checked-live
behaviours.checked: Observed in real Spotify responses; the archive view records the refusal.

behaviours.summary: The user's playlists come at most 50 to a page, from an offset of at most 100,000.
behaviours.label: docs-only

behaviours.summary: Search results come 5 to a page by default, at most 10.
behaviours.label: docs-only

behaviours.summary: Another user's playlist answers with its details but not its items, and its items are a 403.
behaviours.label: docs-only

behaviours.summary: A write takes at most 100 URIs.
behaviours.label: docs-only

behaviours.summary: A write naming a track Spotify does not have is refused with a 400.
behaviours.label: docs-only

behaviours.summary: Removing a URI removes every occurrence of it.
behaviours.label: docs-only

behaviours.summary: Adding at a position inserts there; without one, at the end.
behaviours.label: docs-only

behaviours.summary: Change Playlist Details answers 200 with no body.
behaviours.label: docs-only

behaviours.summary: A Development Mode app gets no email, country, product, followers or explicit-content setting for the user, and no popularity or markets for a track.
behaviours.label: docs-only

behaviours.summary: Audio features are a 403 for a Development Mode app.
behaviours.label: docs-only

behaviours.summary: The endpoints removed for Development Mode apps (Get Several Tracks, Create Playlist for a user ID) are not served; the fake answers 404.
behaviours.label: docs-only
behaviours.note: Only the read is replayed: the removed create would make a playlist if it still worked.

behaviours.summary: A write needs playlist-modify-public or -private for the playlist's visibility, a create the one for the new playlist's; without it, a 403.
behaviours.label: docs-only
behaviours.why: Needs a token granted fewer scopes than shuffify asks for; a replay has the one token.

behaviours.summary: Without playlist-read-private, the user's playlists list only the public ones.
behaviours.label: docs-only
behaviours.why: Needs a token granted fewer scopes than shuffify asks for; a replay has the one token.

behaviours.summary: Redirect URIs are HTTPS, or HTTP on a loopback IP literal, never localhost.
behaviours.label: docs-only
behaviours.why: Spotify's authorize page decides it; a Web API replay does not drive a login.

behaviours.summary: A refresh may answer without a new refresh token; the client keeps the old one.
behaviours.label: docs-only
behaviours.why: Token exchange happens before a replay starts, outside the Web API.

behaviours.summary: Older responses name a playlist's items tracks, and each item's track track.
behaviours.label: docs-only
behaviours.why: An older shape Spotify cannot be asked to answer in.

behaviours.summary: A public playlist's embed page carries it in a __NEXT_DATA__ script, as entity.trackList.
behaviours.label: checked-live
behaviours.checked: On demand (.github/workflows/live-integration.yml): reads real embed and public pages, no credentials.
behaviours.why: A public web page, not a Web API call; the live integration tests replay it.

behaviours.summary: A rate-limited call is a 429 that normally carries Retry-After in seconds; the limit counts calls over a rolling 30-second window.
behaviours.label: docs-only
behaviours.why: Spotify cannot be made to answer this way on demand; the fake answers it as an armed fault (faults.py).

behaviours.summary: A spent quota is a 429 whose error object carries "reason": "QUOTA_EXCEEDED".
behaviours.label: docs-only
behaviours.why: Spotify cannot be made to answer this way on demand; the fake answers it as an armed fault (faults.py).

behaviours.summary: 500, 502 and 503 can answer any endpoint, in the same error shape.
behaviours.label: docs-only
behaviours.why: Spotify cannot be made to answer this way on demand; the fake answers it as an armed fault (faults.py).
